stories.headline: COREWEAVE SURGES 25% ON BEAT-AND-RAISE QUARTER, LIGHTING UP THE AI TRADE
stories.body: CoreWeave jumped about 24.7% to $60.77 after reporting roughly $3.66 billion in quarterly revenue, above its own $3.45-3.6 billion guidance, and raising its full-year 2026 outlook, easing fears that AI-infrastructure spending was outrunning demand. Every member of the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed higher as the report rippled across chip and cloud names.
stories.explain: CoreWeave builds data centers on debt financed against the GPUs themselves, so a beat on revenue only matters if it proves the signed contract backlog is converting into cash fast enough to cover that borrowing cost; today's raise did exactly that. Because the stock is a bellwether for how Wall Street is pricing the entire neocloud/AI-capex complex, one clean print was enough to override a day-old narrative about rates threatening that trade.

stories.headline: S&P 500 JUMPS 1.3%, NASDAQ 100 GAINS 2.3% AS TECH REVERSES TUESDAY'S HOT-CPI SELLOFF
stories.body: The S&P 500 climbed 1.29% to 7,619 and the Nasdaq 100 rallied 2.30% to 28,374 on Veterans Day, with advancers outnumbering decliners on both the NYSE and Nasdaq, recovering most of Tuesday's inflation-driven slide. The Dow added about 0.5% while the Russell 2000 gained roughly 0.9%, a broader move than Tuesday's narrow tech-led drop.
stories.explain: Tuesday's selloff was priced almost entirely off a higher discount-rate story from hot CPI; today's rally shows that when a company-specific catalyst like CoreWeave's print changes the earnings side of the valuation equation, it can outweigh a one-day move in rate expectations even without any new data lowering those odds. That the move was broad, not just mega-cap tech, suggests short-covering and sector-wide repositioning in AI-adjacent names amplified the bounce beyond CoreWeave's own market cap.

stories.headline: DECEMBER HIKE ODDS HOLD NEAR 82-85% UNDER WARSH DESPITE TODAY'S RISK-ON RALLY
stories.body: Fed funds futures continue to price a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 FOMC meeting as the most likely outcome, with CME-style odds still in the 82-85% range after Tuesday's hot core CPI, even as equities rallied hard today. The Treasury cash market was closed for the Veterans Day holiday, so today's repricing happened entirely through equities and futures.
stories.explain: A stock rally and elevated hike odds are not actually contradictory: equities are pricing a specific company's improving cash flows while rate futures are pricing the macro path, and the two only clash directly when a hawkish surprise threatens valuations broadly rather than one sector's earnings. That the cash Treasury market was shut today is a reminder that fed funds futures and SOFR futures, which did trade, are what let the market keep repricing hike odds even on a bond-market holiday.

stories.headline: NVIDIA'S BOARD PROBE INTO HUANG'S FOREIGN-INTELLIGENCE TIES REMAINS OPEN AS CHIPS RALLY ANYWAY
stories.body: The independent board committee investigating CEO Jensen Huang's reported ties to a foreign-intelligence effort has produced no findings yet, with a closed-door briefing for lawmakers reportedly sought for Nov. 18, even as Nvidia and peers rode today's CoreWeave-driven chip rally higher.
stories.explain: The probe is a key-person governance risk that trades somewhat independently of the sector's demand story, which is why Nvidia can rally with the rest of the semiconductor complex on a day like today while the overhang from the investigation stays priced in as a separate tail risk rather than disappearing. Because Nvidia carries one of the largest single weights in both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100, any adverse finding from the probe would have an outsized, mechanical effect on both indices well beyond its own market-cap share.

stories.headline: GOLD SLIPS, DOLLAR FIRMS AS RATE-HIKE PRICING HOLDS; OIL EDGES LOWER ON A THIN HOLIDAY TAPE
stories.body: Gold fell about 1.47% to roughly $3,994 an ounce and the DXY dollar index rose 0.63% to 102.90 as elevated December hike odds kept real-rate expectations firm, while WTI crude slipped about 0.25% toward $86 a barrel on a session thinned out by the Veterans Day bond-market closure.
stories.explain: Gold carries no yield, so when the market keeps a hike priced at 82-85% for December, the opportunity cost of holding it rises even without a new catalyst, which is the direct link to today's drop; a firmer dollar compounds that by making gold costlier for non-dollar buyers. Oil's small decline despite the same hawkish backdrop suggests crude traders are reading today mainly as a rates and dollar story rather than a fresh demand signal, since actual physical and futures activity was lighter than normal with Treasury desks closed.

watchlist: October PPI due Friday, Nov. 13 at 8:30 AM ET — will show whether CPI's hot core reading is confirmed further upstream in the supply chain
Fed's Dec. 8-9 FOMC meeting — hike odds near 82-85% under Chair Kevin Warsh after Tuesday's hot CPI, even as today's equity rally shows risk appetite intact
Nvidia board's investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's foreign-intelligence ties — still open; a closed-door Capitol Hill briefing has reportedly been requested for Nov. 18
10-year Treasury yield near 5.00% (cash market closed today for Veterans Day) — a push through 5% would tighten financial conditions heading into December
AI-infrastructure earnings read-through — CoreWeave's beat-and-raise sets the bar for upcoming hyperscaler and neocloud capex updates

deepDive.title: CoreWeave's Beat-and-Raise and the Cost-of-Capital Squeeze on AI Infrastructure
content: Today's rally was led by CoreWeave surging roughly 24.7% to $60.77 after beating its own Q3 revenue guidance and raising its 2026 outlook, pulling the Nasdaq 100 up 2.3% just a day after a hot CPI print sent the same stocks lower on fear of a December Fed hike. Why would one earnings beat so easily override a macro narrative pointing toward higher-for-longer rates? The answer lies in how AI-infrastructure 'neoclouds' like CoreWeave are financed, and how directly that financing cost is tied to the exact rate path the CPI report was moving.

CoreWeave's model is capital intensive: it borrows heavily, often using GPUs themselves as loan collateral, to build data centers ahead of signed multiyear contracts with hyperscalers and AI labs, then recognizes revenue as those contracts run. Two numbers matter every quarter: whether revenue and backlog are growing at the modeled pace, and what it costs to carry the debt funding the build-out. With December hike odds near 82-85%, every added point of short rates raises the cost of CoreWeave's floating-rate and refinanced debt. A revenue beat and raised guidance signal the backlog is converting to cash fast enough to outrun that rising financing cost, which is what cut through today's rate noise.

What's easy to miss is that the market increasingly prices CoreWeave less like a software cloud business and more like a leveraged real-asset play, similar to how airlines get priced against fuel costs and lease rates rather than passenger volume alone. A useful historical parallel is the 2000 telecom build-out, when debt-financed capacity expansion also outran near-term revenue; carriers that could only tell a demand story, without proof that backlog was converting into cash faster than financing costs were rising, were the ones that failed once credit tightened. CoreWeave's quarter mattered precisely because it demonstrated that backlog-to-cash conversion, not just a demand headline.

For the next catalysts, Friday's PPI print and the Dec. 8-9 FOMC decision, the lesson is that AI-infrastructure equities will keep reacting less to the rate decision itself and more to whether individual companies' cash conversion outpaces whatever financing cost that decision implies. A December hike that lands as expected, alongside CoreWeave-style beats from upcoming hyperscaler capex updates, is digestible for this trade. A hike paired with a hawkish 2027 dot-plot surprise, without matching cash-flow beats across the sector, is the combination most likely to end this rally rather than extend it.
